metadata.repo_type_justification: Python application source with Lambda entry points, SAM IaC provisioning AWS resources (DynamoDB, Lambda, API Gateway), and a single deployable service.
metadata.archetype_justification: DynamoDB writes for charges and refunds, POST endpoints creating persistent entities, owns a ledger table with user-specific data (charge IDs, refund records).

top_gaps.title: Deployment Strategy
top_gaps.gap: Direct-to-production deployment with no canary or blue/green traffic shifting
top_gaps.impact: High risk of regressions reaching all users; no safe rollout mechanism

top_gaps.title: Async vs Sync Communication
top_gaps.gap: No async patterns for cross-service state propagation
top_gaps.impact: Payment events not emitted to downstream consumers

top_gaps.title: Resource Tagging Governance
top_gaps.gap: No tags on any AWS resource in IaC
top_gaps.impact: Cannot track costs, ownership, or environment for this service

top_gaps.title: Application Security Pipeline
top_gaps.gap: No SAST, dependency scanning, or security validation in CI/CD
top_gaps.impact: Vulnerabilities in dependencies or code reach production undetected

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: Build/test automated but deployment is manual
top_gaps.impact: Deployment bottleneck; error-prone manual sam deploy to production

findings.title: No workflow orchestration for multi-step payment operations
findings.description: Payment operations involve multi-step logic (idempotency check, ledger write, idempotency record) handled entirely in application code via _idempotent_put(). No dedicated orchestration service (Step Functions, Temporal) is used.
findings.gap: Multi-step payment operations coordinated in code with no dedicated orchestration service. Will not scale to more complex flows.
findings.recommendation: Consider AWS Step Functions for multi-step payment workflows if the service expands to include settlement, webhook delivery, or multi-party coordination.

findings.title: No messaging infrastructure for payment event emission
findings.description: No messaging infrastructure (SQS, SNS, EventBridge) configured. Payment state changes (charge created, refund created) are not emitted as events to downstream consumers.
findings.gap: A stateful-crud payments service should emit domain events for cross-service state propagation. Downstream systems cannot react to payment events.
findings.recommendation: Add EventBridge for domain event emission on state changes. Publish payments.charge.created and payments.refund.created events after successful writes.

findings.title: No VPC endpoints for DynamoDB access
findings.description: Serverless architecture provides inherent service-level isolation with OAuth2 auth and least-privilege IAM. However, no VPC endpoints or PrivateLink configured for DynamoDB access.
findings.gap: Lambda-to-DynamoDB traffic traverses AWS network backbone but not via a VPC endpoint.
findings.recommendation: For enhanced security posture, configure Lambda within a VPC with a DynamoDB VPC Gateway Endpoint.

findings.title: PITR enabled but no cross-region backup or restore testing
findings.description: DynamoDB has Point-in-Time Recovery enabled with 35-day retention. No cross-region backup replication or documented restore testing.
findings.gap: No cross-region backup replication. No documented or automated restore testing procedure.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS Backup with cross-region copy rules. Document and periodically test the PITR restore procedure.

findings.title: Operational resources (alarms, dashboards) not in IaC
findings.description: SAM template covers primary resources (Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway). CloudWatch alarms and dashboards referenced in RUNBOOK are not defined in IaC.
findings.gap: CloudWatch alarms and dashboards are manually created. Operational resources outside IaC governance.
findings.recommendation: Add AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm and AWS::CloudWatch::Dashboard resources to the SAM template.

findings.title: No automated deployment in CI/CD pipeline
findings.description: GitHub Actions pipeline automates build and test (ruff, mypy, OpenAPI validation, pytest) but has no deploy stage. Production deployment is manual via sam deploy.
findings.gap: No automated deployment. Pipeline stops at test. Manual sam deploy to production.
findings.recommendation: Add deployment stages using SAM Pipelines or CodePipeline with environment promotion and automated rollback.

findings.title: All communication synchronous with no async patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP request/response. No message publishing, no event emission, no queue consumers. Payment state changes communicated only via synchronous API response.
findings.gap: A stateful-crud payments service should emit domain events asynchronously for cross-service state propagation. No async communication patterns exist.
findings.recommendation: Implement event-driven patterns using Amazon EventBridge. Emit payments.charge.created and payments.refund.created events after successful state changes.

findings.title: API versioning exists but no backward compatibility policy
findings.description: Consistent URL-path versioning with /v1/ across all endpoints. OpenAPI spec version tracks API version (1.4.0). Only one version exists.
findings.gap: No explicit backward compatibility policy or version deprecation documentation. Strategy untested with version transitions.
findings.recommendation: Document a versioning policy covering backward compatibility guarantees, deprecation timeline, and migration guidance.

findings.title: No dynamic service discovery mechanism
findings.description: API endpoint URL output from CloudFormation. Consumers configure the URL via environment variables. No Cloud Map, Consul, or service mesh for dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: No dynamic service discovery. Consumers must configure the API Gateway URL statically.
findings.recommendation: Register the API in AWS Cloud Map or use a stable custom domain (Route 53 + API Gateway custom domain) to decouple consumers.

findings.title: AWS-managed encryption without customer-managed KMS keys
findings.description: DynamoDB SSE enabled with AWS-managed encryption (default key). All data at rest is encrypted but no customer-managed KMS key specified.
findings.gap: Using AWS-managed encryption rather than customer-managed KMS keys. No control over key rotation policy or custom access policies.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to a customer-managed KMS key with defined rotation policy for fine-grained access control and key usage auditing.

findings.title: No vulnerability scanning for Lambda deployment package
findings.description: Lambda runtime auto-patched by AWS. Python 3.12 and arm64. No vulnerability scanning tool configured for dependency packages.
findings.gap: No dependency vulnerability scanning. Dependencies not scanned for known CVEs.
findings.recommendation: Add pip-audit or AWS Inspector Lambda scanning to detect vulnerabilities in Python dependencies.

findings.title: No security scanning in CI/CD pipeline
findings.description: No SAST (Bandit, Semgrep), no dependency scanning (pip-audit, Safety, Dependabot), no security validation in pipeline. Only ruff linting and mypy type checking.
findings.gap: Complete absence of security validation. Vulnerable dependencies or insecure code patterns reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add pip-audit for dependency scanning and bandit for Python SAST. Configure Dependabot. Add security gate blocking on critical findings.

findings.title: No formal SLO definitions
findings.description: RUNBOOK defines alarm thresholds implying SLO targets (5xx > 1%, throttle) but no formal SLO definitions with error budgets exist.
findings.gap: No formal SLOs. Alarm thresholds are not expressed as SLO objectives with error budgets or burn-rate alerting.
findings.recommendation: Define formal SLOs: availability 99.95%, p99 latency < 500ms. Implement error budget tracking with burn-rate alerts.

findings.title: Incomplete business metrics coverage
findings.description: ChargeCreated metric published via Powertools Metrics. Missing refund metrics, revenue tracking, failure-reason breakdowns.
findings.gap: Only ChargeCreated metric published. Missing RefundCreated, ChargeAmount, per-currency breakdowns, failure reasons.
findings.recommendation: Add business metrics for refund operations, charge amounts, failure reasons, and idempotency cache hit rates.

findings.title: Static threshold alerting only
findings.description: Static threshold alarms defined in RUNBOOK (5xx > 1%, throttle, idempotency-conflict > 10/min). No CloudWatch anomaly detection.
findings.gap: All alerting uses fixed thresholds. No anomaly detection for gradual degradation or novel failure modes.
findings.recommendation: Enable CloudWatch Anomaly Detection on error rates and p99 latency. Configure composite alarms.

findings.title: Direct-to-production deployment with no staged rollout
findings.description: Manual sam deploy directly to production. No canary, no blue/green, no traffic shifting. No CodeDeploy integration. No automated rollback.
findings.gap: Every deployment goes directly to 100% of production traffic. No mechanism to catch regressions before they affect all users.
findings.recommendation: Add DeploymentPreference: { Type: Canary10Percent5Minutes } to Lambda functions for CodeDeploy traffic shifting with automatic rollback on alarm triggers.

findings.title: Tests use mocks rather than integration testing
findings.description: Three pytest tests cover idempotency and auth scope using mocked DynamoDB (ledger_stub fixture). No integration tests against real infrastructure or emulators.
findings.gap: No true integration tests. Tests verify handler logic in isolation but not DynamoDB operations, IAM permissions, or API Gateway routing.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests using DynamoDB Local or SAM local invoke to validate actual AWS service interactions.

findings.title: Runbooks are documentation only, not automated
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md has structured incident response documentation. However, runbooks are human-readable only — no automated remediation via SSM Automation or Step Functions.
findings.gap: Incident response requires manual execution of documented steps. No self-healing patterns.
findings.recommendation: Convert high-frequency procedures to SSM Automation documents. Start with auto-rollback on sustained 5xx rate increase.

findings.title: Observability ownership documented but not enforced
findings.description: RUNBOOK references specific dashboards, alarms with actions, and escalation to Payments Platform team. Service name consistently 'payments' across all observability tools.
findings.gap: No CODEOWNERS file. No team tags on AWS resources. Ownership documented but not enforced through tooling.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS file. Add team/owner tags to AWS resources in IaC.

findings.title: No resource tags on any AWS resource
findings.description: No tags on any resource in the SAM template. DynamoDB table, Lambda functions, and API Gateway have no Tags property.
findings.gap: Complete absence of resource tagging. Cannot track costs, ownership, or environment.
findings.recommendation: Add Tags to all resources via SAM Globals: Service, Team, Environment, CostCenter at minimum.

evaluations.title: Managed Compute
evaluations.reason: All compute on Lambda (serverless). No EC2.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB fully managed with PITR and SSE.

evaluations.title: API Entry Point
evaluations.reason: API Gateway with OAuth2 auth, request validation, and tracing.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: All services inherently multi-AZ (Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway).

evaluations.title: Programming Languages
evaluations.reason: Python 3.12 with aws-lambda-powertools and boto3 (modern stack).

evaluations.title: Monolith vs Microservices
evaluations.reason: Single-purpose microservice with clear boundaries and OpenAPI contract.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: All operations complete within milliseconds (DynamoDB single-item puts). No operations exceed 30 seconds.

evaluations.title: Unstructured Data Storage
evaluations.reason: Service handles only structured data. No unstructured data surface.

evaluations.title: Unified Data Access Layer
evaluations.reason: All DynamoDB access centralized in app.py through single table reference.

evaluations.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB is versionless managed service. No EOL risk.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: No stored procedures. All business logic in Python application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Application-level IaC only. CloudTrail is an account-level concern belonging in foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: API Authentication
evaluations.reason: OAuth2 client-credentials via Cognito Lambda authorizer on all endpoints.

evaluations.title: Centralized Identity Integration
evaluations.reason: Amazon Cognito as centralized IdP for OAuth2 client-credentials.

evaluations.title: Secrets Management
evaluations.reason: No secrets needed — IAM roles and OAuth2 tokens. No hardcoded credentials.

evaluations.title: Distributed Tracing
evaluations.reason: End-to-end X-Ray tracing with Powertools Tracer and X-Correlation-Id propagation.
